title: AMD RDNA 4 Radeon 9000 Series GPU
problem: Consumer and professional GPU workloads demand higher compute throughput and power efficiency; incremental improvements on existing architectures provide limited gains.
motivation: GPU architecture iteration enables better performance/watt, improved cache efficiency, and support for emerging workloads (AI, rendering, simulation).
method: RDNA 4 evolves RDNA 3 with improvements to compute units, cache hierarchy, and memory subsystem. Likely includes increased compute density, optimized for both gaming and compute workloads.
key_novelty: Next-generation consumer/professional GPU architecture balancing performance, power, and versatility across gaming and compute.
contributions: Increased compute unit density and efficiency
Improved cache hierarchy and memory bandwidth
Enhanced support for compute workloads (AI, simulation)
limitations: Specific architectural improvements and performance numbers not in title.
